exposure: Gestational age at induction (37, 38, 39, and 40 weeks)
Parity (nulliparous vs. multiparous with prior vaginal delivery)
cohort: 74,725 obese women in California with term, singleton, vertex, nonanomalous deliveries in 2007.
finding: In obese women, term elective induction of labor may decrease the risk of cesarean delivery, particularly in multiparous women, without increasing the risks of other adverse outcomes compared to expectant management.
mod_finding: Elective induction of labour (eIOL) at 37 weeks was associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery in nulliparous women.
